nodes.description: Nephrin is located at the slit between podocyte foot processes and is the first protein identified there. In kidneys lacking nephrin, filtration slits of various sizes remain but carry no slit diaphragm, and foot processes are fused. The same picture appears in Nphs1-null mice and nphs1-mutant zebrafish. Engagement of the nephrin ectodomain activates Fyn, phosphorylates the nephrin tail and recruits Nck to polymerise actin, so nephrin also couples the junction to the foot-process cytoskeleton.

nodes.description: Biallelic NPHS1 variants segregate with the disease. NPHS1 encodes nephrin, a 1241-residue transmembrane protein of the immunoglobulin family of cell adhesion molecules expressed in renal glomeruli. In Finland two founder alleles, a 2-bp deletion in exon 2 (Fin-major) and a nonsense variant in exon 26 (Fin-minor), account for over 90% of disease alleles; both abolish nephrin expression in the kidney. Outside Finland most alleles are missense. Nephrin's molecular activity is cell-cell adhesion across the filtration slit: it is an immunoglobulin-superfamily adhesion molecule that binds Neph1, and the slit diaphragm is proposed to be a zipper of nephrin molecules from neighbouring foot processes. The DECREASED modifier records the loss of nephrin protein, not a measured activity.
